Do not \\\\\"fix\\\\\" a migrated skill by editing the leftover skill copy; that edit does not reach\\\\n   the agents now reading the memory.\\\\n\\\\n## Hard Rules\\\\n\\\\n- Create and delete apply only to custom (USER) skills \\\\u2014 managed (LEARNED) skills cannot be created or deleted from Chat.\\\\n- To edit a managed skill\\'s content, use `update_skill`. If an existing skill covers a similar domain or purpose, suggest updating it instead of creating a new one. Only proceed with creation if no existing skill is a good fit, or the user explicitly wants a new one.\\\\n2. **Gather requirements** \\\\u2014 purpose, instructions, and whether the skill needs reference files\\\\n   - A skill only needs SKILL.md if the instructions fit in one document\\\\n   - Add reference files when the skill needs: runbook templates, API reference docs, configuration examples, troubleshooting decision trees, or service-specific guides that would bloat SKILL.md\\\\n   - Organize reference files by purpose: `references/` for documentation, `assets/` for templates and config files\\\\n   - Keep SKILL.md focused on the workflow and decision logic; put detailed reference material in separate files that the agent loads on demand\\\\n2. **Generate SKILL.md** with valid YAML frontmatter and markdown body\\\\n3. **Call `create_skill`** with title, content, and optionally resources\\\\n   - `create_skill(title=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\")`\\\\n   - If the skill needs reference files: `create_skill(title=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\", resources={\\\\\"references/guide.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Guide content\\\\\", \\\\\"references/examples.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Examples\\\\\"})`\\\\n4. **Show the user what was created** \\\\u2014 mention the skill name, description, and key steps. Disabled skills remain in the agent space but are not loaded by agents\\\\n\\\\n### Change Agent Type\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to change which agent types can use a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `update_skill_agent_type`** with the knowledge_item_id and the desired agent_types list \\\\u2014 see the tool\\'s `agent_types` parameter for the accepted values\\\\n2. **Report** \\\\u2014 confirm the new agent type targeting\\\\n\\\\n## SKILL.md Format\\\\n\\\\nCreate a valid SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and markdown body:\\\\n\\\\n```markdown\\\\n---\\\\nname: my-skill-name\\\\ndescription: Brief description of what this skill does. Be specific about when\\\\n  the agent should use this skill (minimum 100 characters recommended).\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Skill Title\\\\n\\\\nInstructions for the agent when this skill is activated.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n- Condition 1\\\\n- Condition 2\\\\n\\\\n## Steps\\\\n1. Step one\\\\n2. Step two\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Frontmatter Rules\\\\n- `name`: Required. Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only (max 64 chars). Must not start or end with a hyphen. Example: `rds-throttling-investigation`\\\\n- `description`: Required. Brief explanation of when to use this skill (min 100 chars recommended, max 1024 chars).\\\\n\\\\n### Resource Files\\\\n\\\\nSkills can include reference files alongside SKILL.md. Reference files provide additional context the agent can load on demand. Use resource files when the skill needs supporting documentation, examples, API references, or other supplementary content.\\\\n\\\\n**Allowed file types:** `.md`, `.txt`, `.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.xml`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.svg`, `.webp`, `.pdf`\\\\n\\\\n**Restrictions:**\\\\n- No script files (`.sh`, `.py`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.rb`, `.pl`, `.ps1`, `.bat`, `.cmd`, `.exe`)\\\\n- No `scripts/` directory\\\\n- No files with shebang (`#!`) content\\\\n- Maximum 100 files, 6 MB total\\\\n\\\\n## Example\\\\n\\\\nUser: \\\\\"Create a skill that helps investigate Lambda cold start issues\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n1. This feature helps reduce traffic interruptions from minutes to seconds by enabling TCP endpoints to quickly detect failed connections and establish new TCP flows through healthy targets.
